title: Create a Worker Profile for Payroll
description: Create and validate a worker profile so the worker can be included in payroll runs without missing data or compliance gaps.
prerequisites: You have admin access to worker or payroll settings.
Required worker identity details are available (name, contact information, classification).
You know whether the worker is an employee or contractor before profile creation.
steps: Open the payroll module and navigate to worker management or worker profiles.
Select Create Worker Profile to start a new worker record.
Enter core identity details such as legal name, email, and employee or worker number.
Set worker classification fields, including workerType (employee or contractor) and payType (hourly or salary).
Enter compensation settings including payRate and any required payroll defaults.
Add required address and contact fields used for payroll and HR records.
Review compliance-related fields and confirm required profile elements are complete.
Save the worker profile and verify the worker appears in the payroll worker list.
Open payroll preview and confirm the new worker is selectable for the next payroll cycle.
validations: The new worker appears in worker management with correct classification and pay settings.
No required-field warnings remain on the worker profile.
The worker is available in payroll run or preview selection lists.
commonErrors: Worker profile cannot be saved because a required field is missing.
Worker is saved but does not appear in payroll run selections.
Incorrect workerType or payType causes payroll calculation issues.
recovery: Complete missing required fields and save again.
Reopen the profile and confirm payroll eligibility fields are set correctly.
Correct workerType/payType/payRate values, save, and rerun payroll preview.

faq.question: When should I use employee versus contractor workerType?
faq.answer: Use the value that matches your legal and payroll classification rules so deductions and reporting are correct.

faq.question: How do I confirm this profile is payroll-ready?
faq.answer: Check required profile fields, then verify the worker appears in payroll preview with expected pay settings.

source.workflowInstruction: Targeted remediation guide for failing critical payroll intent
